description.narrative: Improved Peaceful Coexistence and Social Cohesion for conflict - affected Communities in kutum rural areas in North Darfur State.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

description.narrative: - Community level peacebuilding interventions initiatives and social cohesion for peaceful dialogue through specific activities targeted harmonious co-existence strengthened. - Participation of women, youth and marginalized communities in decision-making structures and peacebuilding mechanisms in key political tasks of the transitional period increased.

comment.narrative:
Output 2: Ensure peace dividends for community interdependence and co-existence are delivered through diverse livelihoods options and effective natural resource management:
2. Income Generating Activities (IGAs): - 140 women trained in small business management to help them in their income generating activities. The training covered marketing and sales for fuel-saving stoves, handcrafts, and food processing. Targeting was based on individual participant skills, most of them had an ongoing micro-enterprise. The women also received booster in kind starter kits as per the trade they are pursuing for example food processing material.

2021-2022 Targets:
Output 1: Community-based conflict resolution and reconciliation mechanisms (CBRMs) are in use and working effectively to resolve conflict: - Training of 70 CBRMs members and establishment of 7 CBRMs. - Training of 24 key stakeholder’s village leaders, local government, native-administrative unit to enhance their skills, knowledge and accountability in peacebuilding. - Organize three (3) cross tribal peace building forums. - Mentorship and coaching sessions on a monthly basis for 7 months targeting 140 women and 140 youth to strengthen the role of women and youth in peacebuilding. - Organize sports or cultural events to bring together two (2) different community groups 2 times per village every 3 months.
Output 2: Peace dividends for community interdependence and coexistence are delivered: - Rehabilitation of two (2) boreholes and solar installation. - Construction of one (1) shallow well for agricultural production. - Training of 45 members of the water management committees (WMCs) in the operation and maintenance of water infrastructure. - Training for 80 small-scale farmers in Farmer Field Schools (FFS) and Good Agricultural Practices (GAP). - Training of 60 pastoralists in Pastoralist Field Schools (PFS). - Procurement and distribution of seeds for 1,000 beneficiaries. - Conduct labour market assessment and value chain analysis to identify value creation potential. - Improve job prospects through vocational training and entrepreneurship skills training for 140 young people (18-35 years), as well as people with disabilities. - Training of 14 community-based animal health workers and equipping with veterinary kits. - Construct of one (1) multi-functional centre in Dissa village within the target area. - Training of 140 women in income-generating measures/small businesses (e.g. production, marketing and sales for fuel-saving stoves, handicrafts and food processing). - Establishment of one tree nursery in identified sites within one of the 7 villages. - Demarcation of one (Shringow) migratory route covering 100 kilometers in 3 target villages (Damrat Guba, Dissa). - COVID-19 prevention measures.
Output 3: Women´s organizations, including those representing pastoralist women, empowered to meaningfully participate in local and state-level peacebuilding platforms: - Mapping and establishment of 7 women organizations in the target villages. - Train all 49 executive committee members on fundraising, leadership, financial management, small grants mechanism. - Organize 8 awareness raising sessions during the project period (4 per year) on Gender/GBV and (Child) Protection. - Train 70 young women and girls (10 each per village) on advocacy skills (special focus on pastoralist women).
Output 4: Improved networking, coordination and learning between local and state-level peacebuilding institutions: - Exchange visits between CBRMs and other stakeholders for mutual learning and networking. - Establishment of a Peacebuilding network with linkages to relevant government authorities in El Fasher . - Capacity strengthening of local partner RSD and 7 CBRMs registered as CBOs.

• Seven (7) CBRMs formed - one in each village. With a total of 70 members (42 men, 28 women, 14 youth)/20 are pastoralists and 50 are farmers. • 2 boreholes in Helt Tafa and Erada were selected for rehabilitation • Seven (7) Field Schools established. Five (5) are Farmer Field Schools comprising of 20 farmers each, 11 male and 9 female) and two (2) are Pastoralist Field Schools comprising of 20 male and 10 female). • 7 new women organizations were established and strengthened in the target villages.
